source.publication: US Department of the Interior / Utility Dive

description: A negative US policy shock has impaired offshore wind. The Trump DOI suspended five major leases (Empire, Revolution, Sunrise, Vineyard 1, CVOW) on 2025-12-22 and is paying developers (>$2bn TotalEnergies deal) to CANCEL leases and switch to oil/gas. Developer impairments cascaded: Orsted needs ~$9.4bn to finish two US projects citing 'adverse developments'; Equinor took a $955M Empire Wind impairment; Shell a $996M Atlantic Shores loss. BNEF cut its US offshore deployment forecast from 39 GW to ~6 GW by 2035. The EU side is a separate, milder recovery (111 GW-by-2030 target intact; EU auctions awarded ~17.2 GW in 2025). Directly relevant to wind_energy_offshore as a HEADWIND: there is no positive structural driving US offshore wind — the real levers (WACC, CfD/lease policy, OEM-duopoly economics) are all rate/policy-bound and currently adverse. Registered as a bearish/regime headwind so the sector is flagged policy-impaired rather than left to score on a momentum-only baseline; the tradable read is EU-only or avoid.
user_notes: Registered 2026-07-01 in the sectors-without-catalyst review. Drives wind_energy_offshore as a bearish policy headwind. relation_to_structural='contradicts' so the catalyst_scorer records it WITHOUT adding a positive alignment term — correct for a headwind: an impaired sector should not be lifted in the heatmap (its alignment stays N/A/baseline). Long 180d half-life: this is a durable policy regime, not a one-shot shock. The EU offshore recovery is a DIFFERENT investor base — do not treat this as EU-bearish; if a EU-only offshore vehicle is used, model that separately. Re-check on any DOI lease reinstatement or a 2028 US administration shift.
